question: What happens to the senses when the yogin moves into another body?
premises: Ordinary death involves the senses merging inward.
The yogin's transfer is controlled and follows the mind.
A subtle continuity is maintained in the transition.
inference: Therefore, in moving to another body there is no inward merging of the senses; instead a subtle body-like continuity arises.
uncertainties: madhyagaṃ melanam is compressed; it likely refers to the senses withdrawing into an inner center.
plain_english: Therefore, when he moves into another body, there is no inward merging of the senses as in ordinary death. Instead, a subtle continuity arises again, like a body.
